problem: The sentence is corrupted: "h2 − ab 2 − ab = 0 is semidefinite" repeats itself and reads as nonsense, so the student cannot tell what the condition is.
fix: "The discriminant h² − ab helps: h² − ab < 0 means the quadratic part is definite; h² − ab = 0 means it is semidefinite; h² − ab > 0 means it is indefinite."

problem: Only two of the three discriminant cases are given. The definite case h² − ab < 0 is never stated, though the ellipse discussion just before it depends on that case.
fix: Add the missing case: h² − ab < 0 means the two eigenvalues have the same sign, so the quadratic part is definite and the curve is an ellipse type.

problem: "The signs of its eigenvalues are p and q" is wrong: p and q are counts of positive and negative eigenvalues, not the signs themselves. A student may read p as a sign.
fix: "p is the number of positive eigenvalues and q is the number of negative eigenvalues of this 2×2 matrix."

problem: "gives an ellipse, or an imaginary ellipse or a single point when no real points satisfy the equation" attaches the no-real-points condition to the single point too, but a single point does have a real solution.
fix: "Definite gives an ellipse, or an imaginary ellipse (no real points at all), or a single point (one real point)."

problem: The node labelled "indefinite" carries the note "conic: ellipse". That pairs two different things: the 3-variable form is indefinite, while the ellipse comes from the separate 2-variable quadratic part x² + 4y².
fix: Give the conic its own node after the sign-count nodes, for example "conic x² + 4y² = 4 → p = 2, q = 0 → ellipse", and leave the "indefinite" node with no conic note.

problem: The lead calls index = p the "common convention". Many textbooks define the index (index of inertia) as the number of negative squares, so calling p the common choice is misleading even though the chapter later warns about conventions.
fix: Say "index = p (number of positive squares) in the convention used here; some books take the index as the number of negative squares instead".
